entries.18fae298fb9efd4e: In Japan’s temporary staffing business, Recruit Staffing Co., Ltd. and the Staff Service Group are responsible. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥846,884 million (¥846.8 billion), up 5.2% year on year. The annual securities report also states that on June 2, 2026, after the fiscal year-end, these two companies (Recruit Staffing Co., Ltd. and Staff Service Co., Ltd.) were subject to an on-site inspection by the Japan Fair Trade Commission on suspicion of violating the Antimonopoly Act, and that the company cannot currently make a reasonable estimate of the outcome or the amount of the impact.

entries.1a5fbe0a4fb609be: This business is centered on Indeed in the United States, and accounts for more than half of the HR Technology Business. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥801,623 million (¥801.6 billion, up 7.6% from the previous year), and $5.31 billion on a US dollar basis (up 8.8%). The company explains that revenue grew even as hiring demand stagnated because average revenue per 1 job listing on Indeed (US average unit price, US ARPJ) rose 17%.

Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥308,570 million (¥308.5 billion), up 17.8% year on year, the largest increase among the three business areas of the HR Technology Business. In US dollar terms, it was $2.04 billion (up 19.2%).

Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥156,972 million (¥156.9 billion, up 4.5% year on year).
entries.6eace0e57f24eaeb: An area made up of fields such as automobiles, weddings and education. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥113,883 million (¥113.8 billion, up 0.2% year on year).
entries.9496ba61fdd82d38: A business that operates websites connecting users with shops and companies in fields such as beauty, travel, dining and housing, mainly in Japan. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, it changed its name from the Matching & Solutions Business to its current name. Representative services include HotPepper Beauty for beauty, Jalan for travel, HotPepper Gourmet for dining and SUUMO for housing, combined with SaaS (software used over the internet) that helps shops with their work, such as the 13 Air Business Tools, including the payment app Air Pay and the POS register app Air Regi. Fees, in many fields, follow an “Expected Action Volume Plan” based on the number of user actions expected on the site and the cost of acquiring them, and in the beauty field, since January 2026 it has also introduced a “GMV-linked model” under which it receives consideration according to the total value of transactions generated via the site. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥563,584 million, the smallest of the three [[term:segment|segments]], while EBITDA+S was ¥154,976 million (¥154.9 billion, up 13.0% year on year), larger than the Staffing Business, and the EBITDA+S margin was 27.4%. The number of employees was 14,096 as of March 31, 2026.
entries.a26cb2fd94a1712f: This is the HR technology business in Japan, which includes Indeed as well as Rikunabi NEXT, a job-change site, and Recruit Agent, a recruitment service. On April 1, 2025, the human resources field that had previously been in the Matching and Solutions business was moved here. In Japan, through a job distribution mechanism called Indeed PLUS, companies' job postings are automatically distributed to job boards such as Rikunabi NEXT and Townwork, and the annual securities report states that it reaches up to approximately 7-tenths of the users of major job sites in Japan. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥348,225 million (¥348.2 billion), down 4.6% from the previous fiscal year.
entries.ab2cbf2106638232: A business centered on Indeed in the United States, accounting for more than half of the HR Technology business.
entries.ac54539d506d1189: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 rose 28.5% to ¥630.5 billion (¥630,567 million), and profit before tax rose 22.3% to ¥644.6 billion (¥644,618 million).
entries.ae6acaccba644486: A business that dispatches people for roles such as clerical work, manufacturing and light work, and various specialized occupations, to companies. Dispatch staff are recruited and registered in advance, and Group companies select people who match the wishes of client companies, sign employment contracts with them, and then dispatch them. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that a distinguishing feature of this business is that it does not end at placement: dispatch fees, including the wages of dispatch staff, continue to be recorded as revenue while the staff are working, and that because dispatch staff tend to want to work near their homes, “local matching,” with sales bases in each region, is important. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,679,327 million, the largest of the 3 [[term:segment|segments]]. However, EBITDA+S (operating income with depreciation and amortization, share-based compensation expenses and other items added back), which the annual securities report uses as segment profit, was ¥99,744 million (¥99.7 billion), the smallest of the 3, and the EBITDA+S margin on revenue was 5.9%. The fact that revenue includes dispatch staff wages is a premise to keep in mind when comparing the size of revenue with the low margin. It had 13,354 employees as of March 31, 2026.
entries.b2e85c05ec28bc34: A temporary staffing business in Europe, the United States and Australia, which began with the acquisition of the U.S. company The CSI Companies, Inc. in 2010 and has expanded through M&A. In Europe, the company provides staffing services under brands such as Start People, Unique, USG Professionals, Secretary Plus, Bright Plus and Solvus; in the United States, under brands such as Staffmark and CSI Companies; and in Australia, under brands such as Chandler Macleod and Peoplebank. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥856,551 million (¥856.5 billion), down 0.6% year on year.
entries.b49e0061d02a252d: Europe, the United States and Australia
entries.b7acc4b188a0732f: A business that connects job seekers and companies offering jobs, centered on the online job matching and recruitment platform “Indeed.” Indeed has the mission “We help people get jobs” and, according to the annual securities report, holds profiles of more than 665 million job seekers and is the world’s largest job information site, used by 3.5 million corporate clients a year (based on comScore visit figures for March 2026). Companies can post job advertisements, view candidate profiles and arrange interviews, and pay fees either on a pay-for-performance model or a subscription model. Also included in this business are “Glassdoor,” which carries job information and user-posted company reviews; the Japanese job-change site “Rikunabi NEXT”; and the placement service “Recruit Agent.” Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,454,440 million, the 2nd-largest of the 3 [[term:segment|segments]], but EBITDA+S, the segment profit, was ¥549,995 million (¥549.9 billion, up 21.5% year on year), the largest of the 3, and the EBITDA+S margin was 37.7%. The company cites progress in efficiency, including a decrease in personnel costs, as the reason. The number of employees was 18,005 as of March 31, 2026, the largest of the 3 businesses.
entries.b90edd4cc44717fc: Europe, the United States and Australia
entries.ba5283c460a0ee60: The main payers are corporate clients that post job listings, client companies of staffing services, and corporate clients such as hair salons, accommodation facilities and restaurants. The foundation is a structure in which most individual users (job seekers and consumers) use the sites free of charge, while corporate clients pay advertising fees and commissions. The annual securities report states that there is no counterparty accounting for 10% or more of revenue.

entries.e2e31174f3ad0bc6: It provides “Indeed,” which connects job seekers with companies; “Recruit Agent,” a domestic personnel placement service; staffing services in various regions; lifestyle matching sites such as “HotPepper Beauty” for beauty, “Jalan” for travel, “HotPepper Gourmet” for dining and “SUUMO” for housing; and “Air Business Tools” for stores.

entries.f0e2b5229374a89f: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] describes the group as a company that “creates and operates platforms that mainly connect individual users and corporate clients.” In the HR Technology Business and the Marketing & Matching Technology Business, most individual users (job seekers and consumers) use the sites free of charge, and corporate clients pay job advertising fees, performance-based fees, usage fees for business support SaaS and other fees. The Staffing Business differs in that client companies pay staffing fees that include the wages of dispatched staff. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 of ¥3,697,351 million breaks down as HR Technology Business ¥1,454,440 million, Staffing Business ¥1,679,327 million and Marketing & Matching Technology Business ¥563,584 million, and the annual securities report states that there is no counterparty accounting for 10% or more of revenue.
